release.smallest_complete_loop: A visitor opens JW Stone, chooses any real Current Inventory listing or published container, creates or signs into a JW-only Express Account, submits and manages a sealed private USD offer, and an authorized JW operator reviews the masked offer, deliberately reveals contact, and processes container opportunities in highest-offer-first order without exposing competing bids or creating a TradeScout customer account.

requirements.actor: Any public visitor
requirements.trigger: The visitor opens /jw-stone or an existing JW profile destination
requirements.behavior: The new marketplace renders only at /jw-stone while existing JW profile and custom-domain destinations retain their current renderer and behavior.
requirements.constraints: The new route is standalone, reachable, canonical, and has no presentation migration or redirect from the existing profile.
requirements.negative: No code may switch, restyle, redirect, or mutate /u/jw-stone, the JW custom-domain profile, profile editing, inventory routes, or database presentation settings.
requirements.unchanged: All current JW profile appearance, behavior, editing, inventory, Direct Connect, and custom-domain routing remain unchanged.
requirements.acceptance: Route and regression tests distinguish /jw-stone from every existing profile route and the rendered application confirms the separation.
requirements.proof: App routing tests, server route tests, profile regression tests, source diff review, and desktop/mobile route captures.

requirements.actor: Fabricators, builders, designers, and homeowners
requirements.trigger: A visitor begins discovery on /jw-stone
requirements.behavior: The visitor sees First Cut and real supplied catalog selections under the approved Current Inventory heading immediately, can open a stone in one click, and may independently choose a customer path, visual color direction, material, finish, search term, verified origin, or eligible named-stone detail through reversible shareable state.
requirements.constraints: Customer path and every refinement are optional and restore independently from clean public query parameters; invalid values do not discard unrelated valid state.
requirements.negative: No customer-path or color choice may gate inventory, replace the page, start a questionnaire, manufacture another choice, open contact, or expose price values or anonymous internal identifiers.
requirements.unchanged: Existing profile discovery and search behavior outside /jw-stone remains unchanged.
requirements.acceptance: Tests prove initial inventory, one-click detail access, independent URL round trips, invalid-state recovery, and optional refinements without a staged dependency.
requirements.proof: State parser unit tests, component journey tests, and desktop/mobile browser journeys.

requirements.actor: A Fabricator, Builder & Developer, Architect & Designer, or Homeowner who wants targeted help
requirements.trigger: The visitor clicks one compact customer-path control
requirements.behavior: One in-place panel reveals concise source-attributed decision support and a compact rail of validated named JW stones selected by an explicit evidence-safe reason.
requirements.constraints: Guidance uses the exact sources and item rules in data-contract.md; recommended slugs are named, reviewed, catalog-valid, and capped at six; each rail and item shows its factual reason; the closed selector is one toolbar row and the complete expanded guide stays under 520 rendered pixels at 1440 and 390 widths; the complete storefront and its ordering remain present.
requirements.negative: A path cannot become a product, workspace, questionnaire, filter, page replacement, contact action, audience-specific catalog, or claim of suitability, popularity, live availability, future supply, origin, performance, or preference.
requirements.unchanged: Canonical inventory identity, shared cards, galleries, wishlist, filters, and optional Direct Connect boundaries are identical across customer paths.
requirements.acceptance: Focused tests and four browser captures prove exact source links, no more than three knowledge points, no more than six validated named stones, visible evidence reasons, a sub-520-pixel guide with no viewport/min-height styling, no second choice, and an unchanged ordered collection ID list before and after every path click.
requirements.proof: Workspace contract tests, DOM structure assertions, source review, and visual evidence for each buyer.

requirements.actor: Any marketplace visitor
requirements.trigger: Inventory is projected into discovery, cards, details, search, sharing, or contact context
requirements.behavior: The marketplace preserves canonical source identities and images, displays only supported material and finish facts, and keeps synthetic Trending Selection inventory publicly nameless.
requirements.constraints: Explicit source fields remain authoritative; source counts are evidence rather than live availability; multiple verified finishes render by their actual labels.
requirements.negative: No invented name, material, finish, origin, dimensions, quantity, availability, translucency, exclusivity, geology, public price, or internal anonymous label may render or enter metadata, URLs, storage, analytics, or contact context.
requirements.unchanged: The canonical JW inventory module and all source IDs, slugs, images, and verified source facts remain unchanged.
requirements.acceptance: Inventory integrity tests reconcile the current record totals, identities, named and anonymous treatment, forbidden labels, safe request labels, and absence of public price surfaces.
requirements.proof: Catalog projection tests, canonical inventory comparison tests, forbidden-string scans, and rendered named/anonymous evidence.

requirements.actor: A marketplace visitor
requirements.trigger: The visitor reaches the First Cut Exclusives editorial section
requirements.behavior: Intentional upcoming-reveal positions communicate the future collection without representing any placeholder as a stone or an available product.
requirements.constraints: Placeholders are presentation-only and the section is ready for later explicit verified collection assignments.
requirements.negative: Placeholders never enter catalog totals, search, filters, SEO, structured data, URLs, wishlist, or Direct Connect and never receive invented names, images, origins, finishes, IDs, slugs, or availability.
requirements.unchanged: Existing inventory is not reassigned to First Cut and anonymous Trending Selection remains a separate inventory concept.
requirements.acceptance: Tests prove zero placeholder catalog records and no placeholder path into discovery, storage, metadata, or contact context.
requirements.proof: First Cut data-contract tests, DOM assertions, metadata scans, and browser capture of the editorial placeholders.

requirements.actor: A visitor evaluating a stone
requirements.trigger: Canonical inventory supplies an explicit verified country-of-origin value
requirements.behavior: Verified origin appears on appropriate cards, details, designer selections, filters, and shareable state; absent origin remains completely hidden.
requirements.constraints: Origin requires an explicit country, a verified flag, and a source designation; filter options derive only from those values.
requirements.negative: The application never infers origin from names, imagery, quarry associations, descriptions, material type, or general Internet knowledge and never renders an empty or unconfirmed origin label.
requirements.unchanged: Current inventory remains origin-empty until JW supplies verified source values and no production migration is introduced.
requirements.acceptance: Production catalog tests show no origin filter for current data while test-only fixtures prove verified display, filtering, URL state, and rejection of unverified values.
requirements.proof: Origin contract unit tests, fixture-driven component tests, and development-only rendered proof that cannot enter production data.

requirements.actor: A visitor without an account
requirements.trigger: The visitor saves, removes, reopens, clears, or returns to a named stone selection
requirements.behavior: A versioned local-browser wishlist stores stable eligible stone IDs, restores safely on return, shows a count and dedicated selection view, and remains separate from contact.
requirements.constraints: Storage is bounded, minimal, account-free, and resilient to unavailable, full, blocked, corrupt, stale, or removed entries.
requirements.negative: Anonymous items, duplicated facts, public price, automatic contact, email or phone gates, reservation language, and malformed data never enter or break the wishlist.
requirements.unchanged: Existing authentication, carts, profile state, and Direct Connect behavior remain unchanged.
requirements.acceptance: Tests cover save, unsave, clear confirmation, refresh and return restoration, corruption, quota failure, unavailable storage, maximum size, removed inventory, and contact separation.
requirements.proof: Pure storage tests, component persistence tests, and a browser close-or-reopen wishlist journey.

requirements.actor: A visitor reviewing the shared inventory
requirements.trigger: A named or anonymous inventory presentation enters the collection or a named stone enters a recommendation rail
requirements.behavior: Stable image-led cards and details expose only verified facts, safe save eligibility, voluntary inquiry, and an accessible full gallery; customer paths do not relabel or restructure them.
requirements.constraints: Named stones support stable detail sharing and saving; anonymous presentations use only Call for availability where identity is needed and cannot be saved under an internal name.
requirements.negative: No public price, unsupported availability, synthetic identity, mouse-only gallery, incorrect image orientation, or forced contact may appear.
requirements.unchanged: Source image order and canonical inventory identities remain unchanged.
requirements.acceptance: Card/detail tests cover named and anonymous paths, keyboard gallery navigation, save labels, safe inquiry labels, responsive structure, and forbidden copy.
requirements.proof: Component tests, accessibility assertions, source scans, and desktop/mobile card and gallery captures.

requirements.actor: A visitor who deliberately chooses an inquiry action
requirements.trigger: The visitor selects Ask about this stone, Start a Request, or Ask about these stones
requirements.behavior: The existing Direct Connect flow opens only after deliberate contact intent and receives bounded stable IDs plus safe public labels for eligible named selections.
requirements.constraints: Discovery, filtering, details, saving, wishlist opening, and sharing remain contact-free; anonymous requests use no internal public label.
requirements.negative: Saving never opens contact, no automatic message is sent, no hold or reservation is created, and anonymous internal names never enter the handoff.
requirements.unchanged: The existing Direct Connect endpoint, privacy behavior, authentication boundary, and non-JW consumers remain backward compatible.
requirements.acceptance: Tests prove contact only follows explicit actions, single and bounded multi-selection payloads are safe, anonymous labels do not leak, and current Direct Connect regressions remain green.
requirements.proof: Handoff unit tests, Direct Connect regression suite, request-payload inspection, and voluntary-contact browser journey.

requirements.actor: Keyboard, touch, reduced-motion, and small-screen visitors
requirements.trigger: The visitor navigates the compact guidance, collection, refinements, or an overlay
requirements.behavior: Every control has semantic purpose and visible focus, the audience guide remains compact and operable, dialogs remain escapable, galleries support keyboard and touch, filters work at mobile width, and motion respects user preference.
requirements.constraints: The layout is usable near 1440-pixel desktop and 390-pixel mobile widths with adequate image-text contrast and no horizontal overflow.
requirements.negative: No trapped dialog, hidden focus, inaccessible save state, contrast-dependent instruction, hydration warning, or console error is accepted.
requirements.unchanged: Global accessibility and design-system behavior outside the standalone route remain unchanged.
requirements.acceptance: Automated semantic tests and real desktop/mobile keyboard and touch journeys pass without overflow, runtime errors, or warnings.
requirements.proof: DOM accessibility tests, reduced-motion and focus assertions, console inspection, and 1440/390 browser captures.

requirements.actor: A visitor, crawler, or recipient of a shared discovery link
requirements.trigger: The standalone route is requested or shared
requirements.behavior: The server emits an accurate canonical, title, description, social metadata, crawler fallback, and sitemap entry for /jw-stone while the client restores safe discovery state.
requirements.constraints: Metadata uses verified business facts, and the canonical excludes transient filters while share URLs retain safe supported query state.
requirements.negative: Metadata and structured surfaces never expose price, anonymous identities, First Cut placeholders as products, invented origin, internal IDs, or duplicate named-stone pages.
requirements.unchanged: Existing profile canonical, custom-domain, robots, sitemap, and social metadata behavior remain unchanged.
requirements.acceptance: Server and sitemap tests prove the new canonical surface and unchanged profile metadata with forbidden-content scans.
requirements.proof: SSR route tests, sitemap tests, metadata extraction, URL parser tests, and production-build inspection.

requirements.actor: A release reviewer
requirements.trigger: The JW Stone 2.0 branch is considered for publication or merge
requirements.behavior: Focused protections, existing JW regressions, type checking, repository guards, production build, broad tests, and real browser evidence must all be reconciled against the exact commit.
requirements.constraints: The feature may be committed and pushed as a draft, but it is not merged, deployed, migrated, or called visually approved without exact-head desktop and mobile proof.
requirements.negative: No skipped protection, weakened assertion, invented screenshot, production migration, DNS change, main merge, or deployment is permitted as part of this build task.
requirements.unchanged: Production, main, DNS, database schema, and the current JW profile remain untouched until a later explicitly authorized release action.
requirements.acceptance: The final evidence names exact commands, counts, revision, screenshots, diff review, branch, commit, push state, and every genuine blocker.
requirements.proof: Exact-head release gate, git diff and route audits, browser evidence ledger, and draft PR state with no production release.

requirements.actor: A visitor evaluating a real JW Current Inventory listing
requirements.trigger: The visitor selects Make An Offer on a card or detail
requirements.behavior: Every real Current Inventory record, including a publicly anonymous listing, opens the JW Express offer flow with a server-validated safe target reference.
requirements.constraints: The action is distinct from Ask and is present on card and detail surfaces at desktop and mobile sizes.
requirements.negative: First Cut placeholders, unknown identifiers, internal anonymous names, and invented availability never enter the offer flow.
requirements.unchanged: Catalog truth, ordering, wishlist, sharing, Ask, and Direct Connect behavior remain unchanged.
requirements.acceptance: Catalog reconciliation proves exactly every real listing is offerable and no placeholder is; component and browser journeys prove both entry points.
requirements.proof: Catalog contract tests, component assertions, and desktop/mobile browser evidence.

requirements.actor: A person making a private JW Stone offer
requirements.trigger: The person creates or signs into a JW Stone Express Account
requirements.behavior: JW stores a separate account with name, normalized email and phone, business status, optional business name, bcrypt password, verification state, and JW-only host session; onboarding may retain one non-active pending-verification offer until the email is verified.
requirements.constraints: Credentials work on platform and custom-domain hosts while sessions remain host-only; authenticated mutations require JW CSRF state; verification promotes the pending offer to submitted, while an unverified account cannot submit or revise another offer or receive acceptance.
requirements.negative: No TradeScout users row, Passport principal, TradeScout cookie, work-request owner, plaintext credential, raw token, or TradeScout onboarding message is created or reused.
requirements.unchanged: TradeScout authentication and customer records behave exactly as before, including when the same email exists in both systems.
requirements.acceptance: Schema, duplicate-email, cookie separation, authentication isolation, password, CSRF, and rate-limit tests all pass.
requirements.proof: Empty/upgrade migration proof plus focused identity and security integration tests.

requirements.actor: A signed-in JW Express customer
requirements.trigger: The customer submits, revises, views, or withdraws an offer
requirements.behavior: The server stores immutable USD-cent offer versions, one current active offer per account and target, requester-scoped history, idempotency receipts, and audited state transitions; initial onboarding may create a pending-verification version that is not active or operator-visible.
requirements.constraints: Optional posted minimums are enforced server-side; verification promotes the pending current version; revisions supersede rather than rewrite prior terms and use their commit time as the new submitted_at priority timestamp.
requirements.negative: No floating-point money, duplicate active offer, cross-account access, payment, reservation, binding-sale claim, rank, competing offer, or automatic contact is allowed.
requirements.unchanged: Public discovery remains usable without an account until the person chooses Make An Offer.
requirements.acceptance: Ownership, minimum, replay/conflict, revision, withdrawal, concurrency, and terminal-state tests pass.
requirements.proof: Transactional service and API integration tests with exact request/response assertions.

requirements.actor: A visitor or authorized JW operator
requirements.trigger: An operator manages a container or a visitor reaches the Containers section
requirements.behavior: Operators create durable draft container records and explicitly publish or close them; the storefront renders only published truth and an honest empty state otherwise.
requirements.constraints: A container has a stable slug, title, optional verified description/media, currency, optional posted minimum, accepting state, and lifecycle timestamps.
requirements.negative: Repository image counts, slab counts, placeholder copy, or generated records never imply a container, availability, contents, condition, origin, or price.
requirements.unchanged: Current Inventory and First Cut identities remain separate from containers.
requirements.acceptance: Publication, validation, empty-state, close/reopen, and public leakage tests plus browser evidence pass.
requirements.proof: Operator API tests, public contract tests, and desktop/mobile section captures.

requirements.actor: An authorized JW operator processing a container
requirements.trigger: The operator reviews or accepts a current container offer
requirements.behavior: Eligible container offers are current submitted or under-review versions for an accepting container and non-closed account, ordered by amount descending, current-version submission time ascending, and ID ascending; acceptance is allowed only for the highest-priority current offer.
requirements.constraints: Pending-verification, accepted, declined, withdrawn, and expired versions are ineligible; revisions re-enter ordering at their commit timestamp; ordering and acceptance execute from server-owned current versions inside a transaction with target and offer locks.
requirements.negative: Client ordering, stale amounts, manual rank override, private rank exposure, and lower-priority acceptance while a higher eligible offer remains active are forbidden.
requirements.unchanged: Stone offers may be reviewed without an auction rank and all customer views remain sealed.
requirements.acceptance: Tie, revision, withdrawal, close, and concurrent-accept tests prove deterministic order and invariant enforcement.
requirements.proof: Database-backed priority and concurrency integration tests.

requirements.actor: The exact JW owner or a narrowly authorized superadmin or operations principal
requirements.trigger: The operator opens /admin/jw-stone-offers
requirements.behavior: A dedicated queue supports target policy, container lifecycle, masked review, contact decision, status actions, event history, and notification retry.
requirements.constraints: Every mutation records the acting TradeScout staff principal only as an audit actor; it never changes JW customer identity.
requirements.negative: General staff, public users, and JW customers cannot access the queue, full contact, actor IDs, private amounts, or delivery diagnostics.
requirements.unchanged: Existing Admin OS tools and Direct Connect operations remain separate.
requirements.acceptance: Exact-role authorization, masking, transition, audit, and admin browser tests pass.
requirements.proof: Role-scoped operator API tests and rendered admin workflow evidence.

requirements.actor: A JW Express customer or authorized JW operator
requirements.trigger: Account, recovery, offer, or status events require email
requirements.behavior: The same transaction persists redacted outbox work for verification, recovery, confirmation, staff alert, and status notifications; an authorized worker atomically claims due rows after commit, records attempts, and moves exhausted work to terminal failed while operator retry creates new work without altering the account or offer.
requirements.constraints: Email purposes are explicitly allowlisted, branded JW Stone, correlation-safe, and staff alerts omit customer contact details; retries occur after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, and 12 hours using row claims that prevent duplicate delivery work.
requirements.negative: Email failure cannot roll back or erase a saved account or offer, and logs never expose address, phone, token, password, offer amount, or provider secret.
requirements.unchanged: Existing email transport and non-JW purpose behavior remain unchanged.
requirements.acceptance: Mode allowlist, persist-before-send, failure, retry, redaction, and recipient/content contract tests pass.
requirements.proof: Email service unit tests and database-backed outbox integration tests.

requirements.actor: A customer, public visitor, or authorized operator
requirements.trigger: Offer or contact data is read or an operator considers contact
requirements.behavior: Public and requester responses contain no competing private data; operator queues mask contact until a distinct authorized reveal action appends an immutable decision event.
requirements.constraints: Offer visibility is intent only; reveal and offer acceptance are separate decisions and neither initiates payment.
requirements.negative: Submitted amounts, ranks, bidder identities, contact details, account existence, event actors, tokens, or delivery diagnostics cannot leak through APIs, HTML, metadata, logs, errors, analytics, or caching.
requirements.unchanged: TradeScout Intent to Decision Card to Contact law remains enforced without creating a TradeScout customer account.
requirements.acceptance: Cross-account 404, redaction, reveal audit, SSR/metadata, cache, log, and acceptance-with-contact-closed tests pass.
requirements.proof: Privacy contract scans and role-scoped integration tests.

requirements.actor: A JW Express account holder
requirements.trigger: The holder verifies email, resets a password, signs out, or closes the account
requirements.behavior: Durable random hashed one-use tokens support verification and recovery; reset revokes sessions, while closure withdraws active or pending offers and transactionally nulls or irreversibly replaces all direct identity and credential fields.
requirements.constraints: Token consumption is atomic, responses resist account discovery, and retained offer/event audit references only a non-reversible closure-specific pseudonym with no recoverable name, normalized email, phone, business name, password hash, session, or unconsumed token.
requirements.negative: No process-memory token, Math.random secret, reusable token, stale session, orphaned active offer, or identity resurrection is allowed.
requirements.unchanged: TradeScout verification, reset, and privacy workflows are not reused or altered.
requirements.acceptance: Expiry, one-use, parallel-consumption, revocation, anonymization, and deleted-account access tests pass.
requirements.proof: Token, session, and account-lifecycle integration tests.

requirements.actor: A release reviewer
requirements.trigger: The private-offer branch is considered complete or publishable
requirements.behavior: The exact commit must reconcile migrations, focused contracts, existing JW/Direct Connect regressions, typecheck/build, browser journeys, leakage scans, minimum release gate, and independent council review.
requirements.constraints: Draft PR publication is allowed after evidence; merge, production migration, and deployment require later explicit GO.
requirements.negative: No skipped security/law suite, fabricated email/browser proof, weakened assertion, unrelated product edit, main merge, or production mutation is permitted.
requirements.unchanged: Production, main, DNS, existing data, unrelated TradeScout lanes, and current JW behavior remain untouched until authorized release.
requirements.acceptance: The ledger names exact commands, results, revision, environment, browser routes, email mode, known baselines, council findings, and unexecuted production proof.
requirements.proof: Build evidence, git diff audit, browser captures, minimum gate, and documented draft PR.

decisions.statement: JW Stone 2.0 is a separate /jw-stone experience and never a replacement presentation for the existing JW profile.
decisions.authority: Thomas's explicit correction in the governing workstream

decisions.statement: Every published inventory, finish, origin, quantity, availability, and identity claim must be supported by canonical source data; absence stays absent.
decisions.authority: Thomas's explicit inventory and country-of-origin requirements

decisions.statement: JW Stone exposes no seller asking price, submitted offer, private rank, or price-derived public sort; the only allowed public price-related value is an operator-configured offer minimum displayed on its exact target.
decisions.authority: The product owner's explicit 2026-08-11 private-offer request, amending the prior no-public-price rule

decisions.statement: The four customer paths are optional one-click guidance inside one always-visible storefront and change only sourced knowledge, an evidence-linked recommendation rail, and supported fact priority.
decisions.authority: Thomas's direct August 3 correction as product owner

decisions.statement: The first release uses a bounded versioned browser-local wishlist with stable named-stone IDs and no account or contact gate.
Color directions are editorial visual classifications derived from supplied stone imagery and are never presented as geological, material, or origin facts.
decisions.authority: Technical implementation judgment inside the required color-first discovery contract

decisions.statement: This build may end in a durable draft pull request but cannot merge or deploy without exact-head desktop and mobile rendered proof.
decisions.authority: Repository release policy and the user's demand for truthful visual proof

decisions.statement: A JW Stone Express Account is a separate customer identity with no TradeScout users row, Passport principal, shared customer session, work-request ownership, or TradeScout account messaging.
decisions.authority: The product owner's explicit statement that the account is with JW Stone, not TradeScout

decisions.statement: Offers are private sealed commercial intents; customers never see competing amounts, identities, counts, rank, or outbid prompts, and acceptance is not payment or a binding sale.
decisions.authority: The product owner's explicit private-not-against-each-other bidding requirement

decisions.statement: A target may have no minimum or one public enforced minimum; hidden reserves are forbidden.
decisions.authority: The product owner's explicit may-or-may-not-have-a-minimum requirement plus truthful-customer behavior law

decisions.statement: Container opportunities are processed by highest active amount first with deterministic earliest-submission and ID tie breaks, and lower-priority acceptance is server-rejected while a higher eligible offer remains active.

The first release presents published containers in one storefront section without standalone container SEO pages, because the request names a section and no authoritative container content exists yet.
decisions.authority: Technical implementation judgment within the product owner's requested scope

decisions.statement: Offer submission and acceptance do not reveal contact; an authorized staff review and immutable reveal event are required before full contact is returned.
decisions.authority: TradeScout platform law preserved inside the JW-only customer identity boundary

decisions.statement: This release introduces no deposit, checkout, payment authorization, reservation, entitlement, or title-transfer path.
decisions.authority: Bounded interpretation of the product owner's offer request and repository release law
